_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Uganda covering Bunyoro-Kitara, Buganda Kingdom, Speke/Baker source of the Nile, British protectorate, Obote, Idi Amin, Bush War, Museveni/NRM, LRA/Joseph Kony, and oil discovery.

ethnic_groups.name: Baganda
ethnic_groups.notes: Central region; Bantu; largest group; Buganda Kingdom (Kabaka/king); Kampala is in Buganda; Luganda language

ethnic_groups.name: Banyankole (Ankole)
ethnic_groups.notes: Western; Bantu; Ankole Kingdom; Bahima (pastoralist) and Bairu (farmers) sub-groups; Museveni's group

ethnic_groups.name: Basoga
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern; Bantu; chieftaincies; sugar cane region; Busoga Kingdom restored

ethnic_groups.name: Bakiga
ethnic_groups.notes: Southwestern (Kigezi); Bantu; highland farming; no traditional kingdom; egalitarian

ethnic_groups.name: Iteso
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern/northeastern; Nilotic (Eastern); Teso region; farming; second-largest non-Bantu group

ethnic_groups.name: Langi
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern-central; Nilotic (Western); Lira; Milton Obote's group; farming

ethnic_groups.name: Bagisu (Gisu)
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern (Mt. Elgon); Bantu; imbalu circumcision ceremony; cross-border with Kenya (Bukusu)

ethnic_groups.name: Acholi
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern; Nilotic (Western); Gulu; LRA insurgency devastated Acholi region; historically strong in military; chiefdoms

ethnic_groups.name: Lugbara
ethnic_groups.notes: West Nile; Central Sudanic; cross-border with DR Congo; Idi Amin's region (though Kakwa)

ethnic_groups.name: Banyoro
ethnic_groups.notes: Western; Bantu; Bunyoro-Kitara Kingdom (oldest kingdom); Omukama; lost territory to Buganda under British

ethnic_groups.name: Batoro
ethnic_groups.notes: Western; Bantu; Toro Kingdom (broke from Bunyoro 1830); Fort Portal

ethnic_groups.name: Kakwa
ethnic_groups.notes: West Nile; Nilotic; Idi Amin's ethnic group; cross-border with DR Congo/South Sudan

ethnic_groups.name: Karamojong
ethnic_groups.notes: Northeastern; Nilotic (Eastern); pastoralists; semi-arid; cattle raiding; least developed region; warrior culture

ethnic_groups.name: Rwenzururu/Bakonzo
ethnic_groups.notes: Rwenzori Mountains; Bantu; Rwenzururu Kingdom recognised 2009; cross-border with DR Congo (Nande)

ethnic_groups.name: Other (50+ groups)
ethnic_groups.notes: Alur, Madi, Jopadhola, Kumam, Sabiny (Sebei), Bafumbira, Indian/Asian community (~30,000; expelled by Amin 1972, returning); 56 recognised ethnic groups

country_profile.notes_unique: Source of the White Nile (Lake Victoria); Winston Churchill called it 'the Pearl of Africa'; home to roughly half the world's remaining mountain gorillas in Bwindi Impenetrable Forest.

natural_resources.notes: Oil discovered in Lake Albert Rift Basin (~6.5 billion barrels reserves); EACOP (East Africa Crude Oil Pipeline to Tanga, Tanzania) under construction with TotalEnergies; copper-cobalt deposits (Kilembe); coffee (robusta, main export); fertile volcanic soils; Lake Victoria fisheries (Nile perch).

military.notes: Uganda People's Defence Forces (UPDF); Museveni came to power via NRA bush war (1986); UPDF deployed in Somalia (AMISOM/ATMIS — largest contributor), DRC, South Sudan; LRA (Joseph Kony) defeated domestically but remnants in CAR/DRC; ADF (Allied Democratic Forces) operations in eastern DRC.

infrastructure.notes: MTN, Airtel telecoms; NITA-U fibre backbone; landlocked (relies on Kenya/Tanzania for internet cables); boda-boda transport.

debt_aid.notes: EACOP oil pipeline ($3.5B) and Tilenga/Kingfisher oil projects ($10B+) to transform economy; Karuma (600MW) and Isimba (183MW) hydropower dams; Anti-Homosexuality Act (2023) triggered US sanctions/World Bank lending pause; Museveni in power since 1986.

top_universities: Mbarara University of Science and Technology
education.notes: Makerere University historically one of Africa's finest (educated leaders across East Africa); Universal Primary Education (UPE, 1997) boosted enrollment (from 2.5M to 8M+) but quality dropped; Universal Secondary Education (USE, 2007); private school sector large.

diaspora_migration.diaspora_population: 1 million+ (Kenya, South Africa, UK, USA, Canada, Rwanda, South Sudan)
diaspora_migration.notes: Hosts Africa's largest refugee population (~1.5M from DRC, South Sudan, Burundi, Somalia); progressive refugee policy (right to work, land allocation); Bidibidi and Nakivale settlements; Idi Amin-era Ugandan Asian expulsion (1972) created diaspora.
diaspora_migration.immigration_policy: Africa's most progressive refugee policy (1.5M+ refugees hosted); self-reliance model

digital_economy.mobile_money_adoption: Very high (MTN MoMo dominant, Airtel Money)
tech_hubs: Kampala (Innovation Village, Outbox Hub, Hive Colab — Africa's first co-working tech hub)
digital_economy.notes: Mobile money ~65% of GDP in transactions; social media/OTT tax (controversial, introduced 2018 then modified); MTN, Airtel, Africell operators; Hive Colab was first tech hub in Africa (2010); growing fintech (Xente, NALA); SEACOM submarine cable access via Kenya.

geography.terrain: Central plateau; western Rift Valley (Rwenzori 'Mountains of the Moon', Virunga); Lake Victoria (shared); Albert/Edward/George lakes; source of the Nile (Jinja)
geography.notes: Pearl of Africa (Churchill); source of the Nile at Jinja; Rwenzori 'Mountains of the Moon'; half of Lake Victoria; mountain gorilla habitat (Bwindi, UNESCO); landlocked; Lake Albert oil.

economy_extended.notes: Oil discovery (Lake Albert, 6.5B barrels; EACOP pipeline to Tanzania controversial); coffee #1 export; steady growth; Museveni (in power since 1986); young population.

health.notes: HIV success story (from 18% to 5%, PEPFAR); Ebola containment (2022); malaria endemic; village health teams (VHTs) model; Mulago National Referral Hospital.

food_agriculture.notes: Robusta coffee (Africa's top exporter); banana/plantain culture (matoke staple); vanilla producer; fertile land; Operation Wealth Creation programme; Karamoja food insecurity.

energy.notes: Bujagali Dam (250 MW); Karuma Dam (600 MW, 2024 completion); Isimba Dam; Lake Albert oil (6.5B barrels, TotalEnergies/CNOOC); EACOP pipeline (controversial, climate/rights concerns).

transport.notes: Landlocked; Entebbe airport (international gateway); Uganda Railways; SGR planned (Kampala-Malaba); matatu/boda-boda (motorcycle taxis) ubiquitous.

unesco_sites_list: Tombs of Buganda Kings at Kasubi
major_attractions: Source of the Nile (Jinja, white water rafting)
tourism.notes: 3 UNESCO sites; gorilla trekking premium ($700/permit); 'Pearl of Africa' brand; adventure tourism (Jinja rafting); chimpanzee tracking; birding paradise (1000+ species).

human_rights_gender.lgbtq_legal_status: Illegal (Anti-Homosexuality Act 2023, death penalty for 'aggravated homosexuality')
human_rights_gender.notes: Anti-Homosexuality Act 2023 (among world's harshest, death penalty clause); Museveni 38+ years; opposition repression (Bobi Wine); media restrictions; Western sanctions/aid cuts over AHA.

active_conflicts: ADF (Allied Democratic Forces, Congo border, ISIS-linked)
security_stability.notes: UPDF in Somalia (ATMIS/AMISOM, major troop contributor); ADF insurgency (eastern DRC); domestically relatively stable; Karamoja disarmament; Lord's Resistance Army (defeated).

cultural_heritage.film_industry: Growing (Ugawood; Wakaliwood action films cult following)
world_heritage_sites: Tombs of Buganda Kings at Kasubi
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: UBC state; NTV Uganda, NBS (private); Daily Monitor, New Vision; press restrictions increasing
cultural_heritage.notes: Pearl of Africa; kingdoms within republic (Buganda, Bunyoro, Toro, Ankole); bark cloth UNESCO; gorilla conservation success; Wakaliwood creativity.

legal_system.legal_tradition: English common law and customary law
legal_system.sharia_applicability: Kadhi courts for Muslim personal matters (limited)
legal_system.customary_law_role: Significant: LC courts (Local Council), Buganda/kingdom courts, elder mediation
legal_system.notes: 2005 multiparty return after 'Movement' system; 2017 age limit removal (controversial); Anti-Homosexuality Act 2023 (partially challenged in Constitutional Court); ICC warrants for LRA (Ongwen convicted).

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: Youngest population in world (median age ~16); major AMISOM/ATMIS contributor.

current_leader.name: Yoweri Museveni
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: NRM; came to power via Bush War; initially praised reformer; constitution amended to remove term limits (2005) and age limits (2017); anti-LGBTQ+ legislation 2023; in power 39+ years

former_leaders.name: Edward Mutesa II (King Freddie)
former_leaders.notes: Kabaka (king) of Buganda; first president (ceremonial); overthrown by Obote 1966; died in exile London 1969

former_leaders.name: Milton Obote
former_leaders.notes: UPC; Langi; abolished kingdoms 1967; overthrown by Amin; returned 1980; Luwero Triangle atrocities; overthrown again by Okello/Museveni

former_leaders.name: Idi Amin
former_leaders.notes: Kakwa; military dictator; 'Butcher of Uganda'; expelled Asians 1972; estimated 100,000-500,000 killed; overthrown by Tanzanian invasion (Kagera War); died in Saudi exile 2003

former_leaders.name: Tito Okello
former_leaders.notes: Acholi; brief military rule; overthrown by Museveni's NRA

910.name: Early Peoples and Iron Age
910.description: Hunter-gatherer communities; Bantu and Nilotic migrations; development of iron-working and agricultural societies in the Great Lakes region.

sub_clusters.name: Early Hunter-Gatherer Communities
sub_clusters.description: Batwa and other hunter-gatherer communities; Stone Age sites in western Uganda; forest-dwelling peoples.

sub_clusters.name: Bantu and Nilotic Migrations
sub_clusters.description: Bantu-speaking peoples arrive from west; Nilotic (Luo, Acholi, Langi) and Nilo-Hamitic peoples from the north; iron smelting traditions.

920.name: Great Lakes Kingdoms
920.description: Rise of Bunyoro-Kitara empire; emergence of Buganda, Ankole, Toro, and Busoga kingdoms; cattle and banana-based civilisations.

sub_clusters.name: Bunyoro-Kitara Empire
sub_clusters.description: Bunyoro-Kitara as dominant Great Lakes kingdom; Bachwezi dynasty legends; control of salt, iron, and cattle.

sub_clusters.name: Rise of Buganda Kingdom
sub_clusters.description: Buganda emerges as tributary of Bunyoro; gradually expands; kabaka (king) centralised power; maritime control of Lake Victoria.

sub_clusters.name: Ankole and Toro Kingdoms
sub_clusters.description: Ankole (Nkore) and Toro kingdoms; Hima-Iru social stratification; pastoral aristocracies.

930.name: Buganda Expansion and European Exploration
930.description: Buganda becomes dominant power; Arab trade contacts; Speke and Baker seek source of the Nile; religious wars.

sub_clusters.name: Buganda Dominance
sub_clusters.description: Buganda supplants Bunyoro as regional power; standing army; sophisticated administrative system; Arab trade in guns and cloth.

sub_clusters.name: Speke and Baker: Source of the Nile
sub_clusters.description: John Hanning Speke reaches Lake Victoria 1858; identifies source of the Nile; Samuel Baker discovers Lake Albert.

sub_clusters.name: Religious Wars in Buganda
sub_clusters.description: Catholic, Protestant, and Muslim factions battle for influence; Uganda Martyrs 1885-1887; Kabaka Mwanga's resistance.

940.name: British Protectorate
940.description: Imperial British East Africa Company; Uganda Agreement 1900; Buganda privileged position; cotton and coffee economy; path to independence.

sub_clusters.name: IBEAC and Early British Control
sub_clusters.description: Imperial British East Africa Company; Lugard arrives 1890; British protectorate declared 1894.

sub_clusters.name: Uganda Agreement 1900
sub_clusters.description: Agreement between Britain and Buganda; mailo land system; Buganda chiefs become landed gentry; indirect rule.

sub_clusters.name: Colonial Economy
sub_clusters.description: Cotton and coffee cash crops; Asian commercial class; railway extension; north-south development divide.

sub_clusters.name: Buganda Crisis and Path to Independence
sub_clusters.description: Kabaka Mutesa II exiled 1953; returns 1955; Buganda federalism question dominates; independence 9 October 1962.

950.name: Post-Independence Turmoil
950.description: Obote's centralisation; Idi Amin's reign of terror; Tanzanian invasion; second Obote regime; Bush War; Museveni victory.

sub_clusters.name: Obote First Government
sub_clusters.description: Milton Obote PM then president; abolishes kingdoms 1967; 'Move to the Left'; Buganda crisis; increasing authoritarianism.

sub_clusters.name: Idi Amin's Reign of Terror
sub_clusters.description: Idi Amin seizes power; expulsion of 80,000 Asians 1972; State Research Bureau; estimated 100,000-500,000 killed; Entebbe raid 1976.

sub_clusters.name: Tanzania War and Amin's Fall
sub_clusters.description: Amin invades Kagera strip; Tanzania counterattacks and captures Kampala April 1979; Amin flees.

sub_clusters.name: Bush War and NRM Victory
sub_clusters.description: Museveni's NRA/NRM wages guerrilla war from Luwero Triangle; captures Kampala January 1986; 'fundamental change'.

960.name: Museveni Era and Modern Uganda
960.description: NRM governance; economic recovery; HIV/AIDS response; LRA insurgency; oil discovery; multiparty transition; democratic backsliding.

sub_clusters.name: NRM Economic Reconstruction
sub_clusters.description: Museveni stabilises economy; 'no-party' Movement system; structural adjustment; praised as 'new breed' African leader.

sub_clusters.name: HIV/AIDS Response
sub_clusters.description: Uganda's early and effective HIV/AIDS response; prevalence drops from 15% to 5%; ABC campaign; global model.

sub_clusters.name: LRA Insurgency and Joseph Kony
sub_clusters.description: Lord's Resistance Army under Joseph Kony terrorises northern Uganda; child abduction; ICC warrants; Kony 2012 campaign.

sub_clusters.name: Oil Discovery in Albertine Graben
sub_clusters.description: Commercial oil discovered in Lake Albert region; pipeline to Tanzania planned; resource curse concerns; environmental issues.

sub_clusters.name: Democratic Regression
sub_clusters.description: Term limits removed 2005; age limit removed 2017; Bobi Wine opposition; disputed 2021 elections; authoritarian consolidation.
